lesson.title: What are we doing tomorrow?
lesson.scenario: Omar and Lina want to visit Omar’s family after work. They move from an idea to an agreed time.

steps.instruction: Ask about tomorrow’s shared plan, not yesterday’s actions.

answers.meaning: What did you do today? (to Omar)
answers.rationale: This asks Omar what he already did today.

answers.meaning: How are you doing? (casual check-in to Omar)
answers.rationale: This checks in with Omar instead of asking about tomorrow’s shared plan.

answers.meaning: What will we do tomorrow?
answers.rationale: Raḥ plus the “we” form and bukra asks about a shared future plan.

evaluation.correctExplanation: Raḥ plus the “we” form and bukra asks about a shared future plan.
evaluation.incorrectExplanation: This is a possible expression, but it does not meet the request in this situation.

steps.instruction: Omar suggests visiting his own family after work. Speak as Omar.

answers.meaning: Shall we visit my family after work?
answers.rationale: Ahli identifies Omar’s family when Omar speaks; after work supplies the ordering.

answers.meaning: Shall we visit your family after work? (to Lina)
answers.rationale: This would mean Lina’s family, changing whose family they visit.

answers.meaning: I worked, then visited my mother.
answers.rationale: This recounts completed work and a visit rather than making tomorrow’s suggestion.

evaluation.correctExplanation: Ahli identifies Omar’s family when Omar speaks; after work supplies the ordering.
evaluation.incorrectExplanation: This is a possible expression, but it does not meet the request in this situation.
evaluation.retryHint: Omar is speaking, so use “my family.”

steps.instruction: You like the visit idea but still need the time. Ask for it.

prompt.meaning: Shall we visit my family after work?

answers.meaning: How’s your family? (to Omar)
answers.rationale: This asks how the family is rather than when to visit.

answers.meaning: Okay. What time?
answers.rationale: Ayy sāʿa asks for a clock time after accepting the idea.

answers.meaning: Do you want tea or coffee? (to Omar)
answers.rationale: This offers drinks rather than settling the schedule.

evaluation.correctExplanation: Ayy sāʿa asks for a clock time after accepting the idea.
evaluation.incorrectExplanation: This is a possible expression, but it does not meet the request in this situation.
evaluation.retryHint: Ask for the missing clock time.

steps.instruction: The agreed time is six. Give that time.

answers.meaning: At six o’clock.
answers.rationale: Sitte sets six o’clock, matching the agreed time.

answers.meaning: At seven o’clock.
answers.rationale: Sabʿa sets seven, an hour later.

answers.meaning: Tomorrow
answers.rationale: Tomorrow gives the day but not the clock time.

evaluation.correctExplanation: Sitte sets six o’clock, matching the agreed time.
evaluation.incorrectExplanation: This is a possible expression, but it does not meet the request in this situation.
evaluation.retryHint: Choose the time, not only the day.

steps.instruction: Lina confirms: tomorrow, six, Omar’s family. Preserve all three details.

prompt.meaning: Shall we visit my family after work?

answers.arabic: تمام، اليوم الساعة ستة نزور أهلك.
answers.arabizi: Tamām, il-yōm is-sāʿa sitte nzūr ahlak.
answers.meaning: Okay, today at six we’ll visit your family. (to Omar)
answers.rationale: The family and time fit, but this changes tomorrow to today.

answers.arabic: تمام، بكرا الساعة سبعة نزور أهلك.
answers.arabizi: Tamām, bukra is-sāʿa sabʿa nzūr ahlak.
answers.meaning: Okay, tomorrow at seven we’ll visit your family. (to Omar)
answers.rationale: The day and family fit, but this changes six to seven.

answers.arabic: تمام، بكرا الساعة ستة نزور أهلك.
answers.arabizi: Tamām, bukra is-sāʿa sitte nzūr ahlak.
answers.meaning: Okay, tomorrow at six we’ll visit your family. (to Omar)
answers.rationale: The confirmation carries forward day, time, and whose family.

evaluation.correctExplanation: The confirmation carries forward day, time, and whose family.
evaluation.incorrectExplanation: This is a possible expression, but it does not meet the request in this situation.
evaluation.retryHint: Check each detail rather than matching only the family.

steps.instruction: In this plan, the visit follows work. Choose “after work.”

prompt.meaning: Shall we visit my family after work?

answers.meaning: Before work
answers.rationale: This reverses the relationship to work.

answers.meaning: After work
answers.rationale: This places the visit after work finishes.

answers.meaning: At work
answers.rationale: This describes a location or work setting, not the requested sequence.

evaluation.correctExplanation: This places the visit after work finishes.
evaluation.incorrectExplanation: This is a possible expression, but it does not meet the request in this situation.

steps.instruction: Closing exchange, part 1: a new plan uses seven instead of six. Give the new time.

answers.meaning: At seven o’clock.
answers.rationale: Use sabʿa to transfer the timing pattern to the revised plan.

answers.meaning: At six o’clock.
answers.rationale: This keeps the earlier time despite the change.

answers.meaning: Tomorrow
answers.rationale: This gives only the day.

evaluation.correctExplanation: Use sabʿa to transfer the timing pattern to the revised plan.
evaluation.incorrectExplanation: This is a possible expression, but it does not meet the request in this situation.

steps.instruction: Closing exchange, part 2: confirm tomorrow at seven with Lina. Say that you will drink tea together.

prompt.meaning: Shall we drink tea together tomorrow?

answers.arabic: آه، اليوم الساعة سبعة نشرب شاي سوا.
answers.arabizi: Āh, il-yōm is-sāʿa sabʿa nishrab shāy sawa.
answers.meaning: Yes, today at seven we’ll drink tea together.
answers.rationale: This changes tomorrow to today.

answers.arabic: تمام، بكرا الساعة ستة نزور أهلك.
answers.arabizi: Tamām, bukra is-sāʿa sitte nzūr ahlak.
answers.meaning: Okay, tomorrow at six we’ll visit your family. (to Omar)
answers.rationale: This repeats the previous visit plan at six instead of the revised tea plan at seven.

answers.arabic: آه، بكرا الساعة سبعة نشرب شاي سوا.
answers.arabizi: Āh, bukra is-sāʿa sabʿa nishrab shāy sawa.
answers.meaning: Yes, tomorrow at seven we’ll drink tea together.
answers.rationale: This confirms the new day, time, and shared activity.

evaluation.correctExplanation: This confirms the new day, time, and shared activity.
evaluation.incorrectExplanation: This is a possible expression, but it does not meet the request in this situation.
evaluation.retryHint: Keep all three details of the new arrangement.

lesson.unitTitle: Everyday conversations with someone you love

introduction.goal: Suggest a shared visit, ask for a time, and confirm tomorrow’s plan.

line.meaning: Shall we visit my family after work?

line.arabic: تمام، بكرا الساعة ستة نزور أهلك.
line.arabizi: Tamām, bukra is-sāʿa sitte nzūr ahlak.
line.meaning: Okay, tomorrow at six we’ll visit your family. (to Omar)
And afterwards we’ll drink tea together.

expressions.meaning: Shall we visit my family after work?

expressions.arabic: تمام، بكرا الساعة ستة نزور أهلك.
expressions.arabizi: Tamām, bukra is-sāʿa sitte nzūr ahlak.
expressions.meaning: Okay, tomorrow at six we’ll visit your family. (to Omar)

introduction.usageNote: Raḥ points forward to a future action; bukra supplies the day, tomorrow. In raḥ niʿmal, the n- form is “we,” so the question is about a shared plan. You do not need raḥ in every turn: a reply such as “tomorrow at six we visit your family” has a clear future setting from context. Baʿd ish-shughl means “after work”; baʿdēn means “then/afterwards.” A plan becomes clearer when you repeat the day, time, and who you will visit. Read the dialogue, then cover it and reconstruct those three details before practising. Clock times here use a shared evening context; a real arrangement may need you to clarify morning/evening.
introduction.dialectNote: Urban Palestinian teaching target. Ahli is the speaker’s family. When Lina confirms Omar’s proposal, it becomes ahlak, his family as her listener. Niʿmal/nzūr/nishrab are shared actions in these phrases. Raḥ is a future marker here, distinct from past rāḥ, “he went.” Transliteration: ā/ī/ū and ē/ō mark long vowels; ʿ = ع, ḥ = ح, ʾ = glottal stop, sh = ش, kh = خ, gh = غ. Doubled letters are held longer. Jordanian alternatives are not introduced in this unit.
introduction.recordingNote: No reviewed recordings yet. This six-turn transcript is the recording script: Lina uses feminine self-description; Omar uses masculine self-description. Read each speaker’s turns in order, then the practice prompts and answer options as separate clips. Retain the marked address distinctions. A Palestinian speaker and owner must check wording/pronunciation before assets are labeled reviewed. Optional device speech is a variable browser preview, not a dialect model.
